caution_findings.finding: The paper supports weak antibacterial phenotype rows and neuroinflammation/oxidative-stress pathway readouts, but it does not identify a direct bacterial molecular target or bactericidal mechanism.
Figure-only time-course and bar-plot values were not converted into exact numeric mechanism rows beyond values stated in source text.

extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from primary XML/PDF sections and figure captions; not a worker-5 expansion beyond local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ocellatin-K1(1-16) and Ocellatin-K1(1-21) altered hippocampal oxidative-stress markers in mice, with source text reporting reduced nitrite and malondialdehyde and increased superoxide dismutase activity and glutathione.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports antioxidant-status modulation in the tested mouse hippocampus model, not a direct antimicrobial mechanism or a specific molecular binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Both ocellatin fragments impaired LPS-induced NF-kB activation in CHME3 human microglial cells in the source reporter assay context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ocellatin-K1(1-16) and Ocellatin-K1(1-21) at 100 uM with 1 ug/mL LPS challenge
mechanism_claims.limitations: The assay supports cellular NF-kB pathway modulation under LPS challenge; it does not identify the direct peptide binding partner.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Both ocellatin fragments reduced oxidative stress in hippocampal neurons exposed to conditioned medium from LPS-treated microglia.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: hippocampal neurons exposed to microglia conditioned medium after peptide/LPS treatment
mechanism_claims.limitations: The source supports reduced ROS signal in the stated co-culture/conditioned-medium model, not a standalone antimicrobial mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Human erythrocyte hemolysis and AFM morphology/roughness assays support low erythrocyte toxicity for Ocellatin-K1(1-16) and higher membrane perturbation for Ocellatin-K1(1-21) at high concentrations.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ocellatin-K1(1-16) and Ocellatin-K1(1-21) in human erythrocytes
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a toxicity/membrane morphology context for erythrocytes, not a bacterial killing mechanism.
